summary: More than 350 AI executives and researchers, including OpenAI CEO Sam Altman, signed a statement warning that AI poses a risk of extinction on par with pandemics and nuclear war. The statement, published by the Center for AI Safety, urges global priority for mitigating AI risks. Experts also highlight immediate concerns like bias and misinformation, while some argue the existential threat warnings are overblown.

claims.text: More than 350 top executives and researchers in artificial intelligence have signed a statement urging policymakers to see the serious risks posed by unregulated AI.
claims.evidence_quote: More than 350 top executives and researchers in artificial intelligence have signed a statement urging policymakers to see the serious risks posed by unregulated AI, warning the future of humanity may be at stake.

claims.text: The statement says mitigating the risk of extinction from AI should be a global priority alongside pandemics and nuclear war.
claims.evidence_quote: Mitigating the risk of extinction from AI should be a global priority alongside other societal-scale risks such as pandemics and nuclear war.

claims.text: The statement was published by the nonprofit Center for AI Safety (CAIS) on Tuesday.
claims.evidence_quote: published Tuesday by the nonprofit Center for AI Safety (CAIS)

claims.text: CAIS executive director Dan Hendrycks compared the AI industry to an 'AI arms race' that could bring humanity to the brink of catastrophe.
claims.evidence_quote: That could escalate and, like the nuclear arms race, potentially bring us to the brink of catastrophe

claims.text: Hendrycks suggested humanity could go the way of the Neanderthals.
claims.evidence_quote: humanity could go the way of the Neanderthals.

claims.text: The letter coincided with the U.S.-EU Trade and Technology Council meeting in Sweden where politicians are expected to talk about regulating AI.
claims.evidence_quote: The letter coincided with the U.S.-EU Trade and Technology Council meeting in Sweden where politicians are expected to talk about regulating AI.

claims.text: Signatories included CEOs of AI firms DeepMind and Anthropic, and executives from Microsoft and Google.
claims.evidence_quote: As well as Altman, signatories included the CEOs of AI firms DeepMind and Anthropic, and executives from Microsoft and Google.

claims.text: Geoffrey Hinton and Yoshua Bengio, two of the three 'godfathers of AI', also signed the statement.
claims.evidence_quote: Also among them were British-Canadian computer scientist Geoffrey Hinton and Université de Montréal computer science professor Yoshua Bengio — two of the three so-called 'godfathers of AI'

claims.text: Yoshua Bengio said AI has reached the Turing Test milestone, meaning machines can converse with humans in a sophisticated fashion.
claims.evidence_quote: AI development has reached a milestone, known as the Turing Test, which means machines have the ability to converse with humans in a sophisticated fashion

claims.text: Bengio worries AI could lead to automation of trolls on social media, as AI systems have 'mastered enough knowledge to pass as human.'
claims.evidence_quote: Bengio worries the technology could lead to an automation of trolls on social media, as AI systems have already 'mastered enough knowledge to pass as human.'

claims.text: Rahul Krishnan, an assistant professor at the University of Toronto, believes AI regulation is 'still playing catch up' but needs a 'good balance'.
claims.evidence_quote: Krishnan said AI regulation is 'still playing catch up' but there needs to be a 'good balance' to ensure technologies are developed and used safely without hindering improvements.

claims.text: Luke Stark, who studies AI at Western University, says AI systems can exacerbate historical biases around race or gender, affecting marginalized communities.
claims.evidence_quote: If the data AI systems are using exhibit historical bias around race or gender, it's going to get exacerbated, built up and further expressed through the system

claims.text: Stark believes the existential threat warnings have gone overboard, and everyday real-world cases of AI controlling groups are not getting enough attention.
claims.evidence_quote: Stark, however, believes the warnings about an existential threat from AI have gone overboard, at least for now.

claims.text: European Commission president Ursula von der Leyen will meet Altman on Thursday.
claims.evidence_quote: European Commission president Ursula von der Leyen will meet Altman on Thursday.
